brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Four bases on one level (three full, one half) with top covers, cap ends and joint bolts. It is about 36 parts, and the top holds a mug and a pencil cup.
drawer:0#0,-1#cut sits on the cut face of the half base at (0,-1) and faces outward. It holds a pen.

requirements.requirement: Spike where three bases meet, holding a small platform
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 is a mount spike facing up at the corner where bases (0,0), (0,1) and (1,0) meet. It carries the platform-sm accessory.

finish.summary: I built a compact desk unit from four bases on one level: three full bases at (0,0), (1,0) and (0,1), plus a south-half base at (0,-1). It has a drawer, and a mount spike carrying a small platform stands on top at the corner where the three full bases meet. All four bases have top covers. I capped the open faces and bolted the joints. A mug and a pencil cup sit on the top and a pen is in the drawer; I couldn't put a prop on the platform itself, because props can't be placed on a spike. check_build reports no issues and the mesh collision check reads clear. My first layout put the half base inside the corner, where the drawer blocked the spike, so I moved the half base to the outside.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
